P0300.m: The engine computer sees misfires that move around between cylinders instead of staying in one. The engine may shake, stumble or feel down on power. If the check engine light flashes, the misfire is bad enough to overheat the catalytic converter: slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plugs or ignition coils
Low fuel pressure or dirty injectors

P0302.m: Cylinder 2 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 2

P1326.m: On Hyundai and Kia engines, the knock sensor detection system picked up vibration that can point to wearing connecting rod bearings. The car may go into limp mode. Owners are usually told to see a dealer, because this system was added during the brands' engine bearing campaigns.

P2111.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Stuck Open
P2111.m: The electronic throttle is stuck more open than commanded. The car can go into limp mode or act unpredictably.

C1391.m: On Toyota and Lexus models with a powered brake booster (mostly hybrids), the brake computer saw the stored brake pressure falling faster than it should, which points to an internal leak. Braking assist can be affected, so get it checked before driving much.
c: Internal leak in the brake booster/accumulator assembly
Leaking seals in the brake actuator

P0303.m: Cylinder 3 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 3

P0304.m: Cylinder 4 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 4

P0420.m: The catalytic converter on bank 1 isn't cleaning the exhaust as well as it should. The car usually drives normally, but it can fail an emissions test.

P0301.m: Cylinder 1 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 1

P2112.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Stuck Closed
P2112.m: The electronic throttle is stuck more closed than commanded, so the engine loses power and may go into limp mode.

P2138.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D/E Voltage Correlation
P2138.m: The two gas pedal position signals disagree, so the car may go into reduced power or not respond to the pedal.

P0700.m: The transmission computer found its own problem and asked for the check engine light. Another transmission code with the details is usually stored too.
c: A second transmission code that says what failed (the transmission computer has to be read for it)
A shift solenoid or sensor fault

P0463.t: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit High
P0463.m: The fuel level sender reads too high. The gauge can show fuel that isn't there, which risks running out of gas.

P0087.m: The engine isn't getting the fuel pressure it needs. That can cause hesitation, loss of power and stalling, especially under load.
c: Faulty fuel pressure sensor or regulator

P0017.t: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor B)
P0017.m: The crankshaft and the bank 1 camshaft aren't lined up the way the computer expects. That usually points to timing chain or belt problems, so it's worth checking early before it gets worse.
c: Stretched timing chain or jumped belt

P0016.t: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A)
P0016.m: The crankshaft and the bank 1 camshaft aren't lined up the way the computer expects. That usually points to timing chain or belt problems, so it's worth checking early before it gets worse.
c: Stretched timing chain or jumped belt

P052E.t: Positive Crankcase Ventilation Regulator Valve Performance
P052E.m: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) system isn't controlling pressure the way it should.
c: Failed PCV valve or oil separator

P0456.t: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Very Small Leak)
P0456.m: There's a very small leak in the fuel vapor system. The car drives normally.
c: Tiny crack in an EVAP hose

P1450.t: Unable to Bleed Up Fuel Tank Vacuum
P1450.m: On Fords, the fuel vapor (EVAP) system couldn't release vacuum from the gas tank. It's an emissions fault; the car usually drives normally.
c: Blocked EVAP vent valve or filter
Faulty purge valve (some Ford bulletins replace it)

P0720.m: The transmission lost its output speed signal. The speedometer and shifting can act up.

P0171.m: Bank 1 is getting too much air or too little fuel. The engine may hesitate or idle rough.
c: Weak fuel pump or clogged filter

P0316.m: The engine misfired in the first moments after starting. It often shows up as a rough or shaky cold start.

P0014.t: B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Exhaust, Bank 1)
P0014.m: The variable valve timing for the exhaust camshaft on bank 1 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P0299.m: The turbo isn't making the boost the computer asked for, so the car feels slow and may go into reduced power.

P0741.t: Torque Converter Clutch Solenoid Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P0741.m: The torque converter isn't locking up as commanded. You may feel shudder or see higher RPM on the highway.

P0722.t: Output Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
P0722.m: There's no output speed signal from the transmission, so shifts and the speedometer can fail.

P2135.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A/B Voltage Correlation
P2135.m: The two throttle position signals disagree, so the computer cuts power to stay safe.

P0430.m: The catalytic converter on bank 2 isn't cleaning the exhaust as well as it should.

P0011.t: A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Intake, Bank 1)
P0011.m: The variable valve timing for the intake camshaft on bank 1 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P0740.m: The torque converter lockup solenoid has an electrical fault. Fuel economy drops and the car may shudder.

P0128.t: Coolant Thermostat (Coolant Temperature Below Thermostat Regulating Temperature)
P0128.m: The engine isn't reaching normal temperature fast enough. The heater may blow cool and fuel economy drops.

P0008.m: The engine computer sees the cam and crank timing drifting out of line on bank 1. On many engines this is an early sign of a stretched timing chain.
c: Faulty cam phaser or VVT solenoid

P2442.t: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2)
P2442.m: The valve that lets cold-start air into the bank 2 exhaust is stuck open. Exhaust moisture can then reach and damage the air pump.
c: Water or carbon in the valve

P0776.t: Pressure Control Solenoid B Performance/Stuck Off
P0776.m: Transmission pressure solenoid B isn't controlling pressure, so shifts can slip, flare or bang.

P0335.m: The computer lost or can't read the crankshaft position signal. Without it the engine can stall and may not restart.

P2440.t: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2440.m: The valve that lets cold-start air into the bank 1 exhaust is stuck open. Exhaust moisture can then reach and damage the air pump.
c: Water or carbon in the valve

P0172.m: Bank 1 is getting too much fuel. You may smell fuel or see worse mileage.

P0306.m: Cylinder 6 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 6

P0305.m: Cylinder 5 is not firing properly, so the engine runs rough and loses some power. A flashing check engine light means the misfire is serious enough to damage the catalytic converter, so slow down and get it checked right away.
c: Spark plug or ignition coil on cylinder 5

U0100.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the engine computer. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the engine computer

P0730.m: The transmission isn't matching the expected engine-to-wheel speed in some gear, which usually means slipping.

P0340.m: The computer can't read the bank 1 camshaft position sensor. Expect hard starting, stalling or a rough run.

P0101.t: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A Range/Performance
P0101.m: The air flow reading doesn't match what the computer expects. The engine may hesitate, stall or idle rough.

P0455.t: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Large Leak)
P0455.m: There's a large leak in the fuel vapor system. Often it's just a gas cap left loose or off.
c: Purge or vent valve stuck open

U0101.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the transmission computer. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the transmission computer

U0401.m: Another computer in the car received data from the engine computer that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the engine computer

P1299.m: On Fords, the engine got hot enough that the computer turned on its overheat protection, which can shut off cylinders and cut power. Pull over and let it cool.

P0747.t: Pressure Control Solenoid A Stuck On
P0747.m: The main transmission pressure solenoid is stuck on, so shifts can be harsh.

P219A.m: One or more cylinders on bank 1 are getting a different air-fuel mix than the others. The engine may idle rough or hesitate.

P0717.t: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor A Circuit No Signal
P0717.m: There's no input speed signal from the transmission.

P2106.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Limited Power
P2106.m: The computer found a throttle problem and put the car in limp mode with reduced power.

P0010.t: A Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Intake, Bank 1)
P0010.m: The variable valve timing for the intake camshaft on bank 1 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P0174.m: Bank 2 is getting too much air or too little fuel.
c: Weak fuel pump or clogged filter

P0442.t: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Small Leak)
P0442.m: There's a small leak in the fuel vapor system.

P0706.t: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0706.m: The gear selector position signal doesn't make sense. Shifting and starting can act up.

P0705.t: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit (PRNDL Input)
P0705.m: The computer can't tell which gear the shifter is in. The car may not start, or may show the wrong gear.

P0401.t: Exhaust Gas Recirculation A Flow Insufficient Detected
P0401.m: Not enough exhaust gas is being sent back into the engine. It can cause pinging and higher emissions.

P0012.t: A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded (Intake, Bank 1)
P0012.m: The variable valve timing for the intake camshaft on bank 1 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P0707.t: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Low
P0707.m: The gear selector position signal is too low.

P061B.t: Internal Control Module Torque Calculation Performance
P061B.m: The engine computer's two torque calculations don't match, so it may cut power for safety.

P0018.t: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 2 Sensor A)
P0018.m: The crankshaft and the bank 2 camshaft aren't lined up the way the computer expects. That usually points to timing chain or belt problems, so it's worth checking early before it gets worse.
c: Stretched timing chain or jumped belt

P0217.m: The engine is overheating. Pull over safely and shut it off: driving an overheating engine can warp or crack it.

P0441.t: Evaporative Emission System Incorrect Purge Flow
P0441.m: Fuel vapor isn't being drawn into the engine the way it should.

P2716.m: Transmission pressure solenoid D has an electrical fault.

U0121.t: Lost Communication With Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) Control Module
U0121.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the anti-lock brake (ABS) module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the anti-lock brake (ABS) module

U0415.t: Invalid Data Received From Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) Control Module
U0415.m: Another computer in the car received data from the anti-lock brake (ABS) module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the anti-lock brake (ABS) module

P1285.m: On Fords, the cylinder head temperature sensor saw the engine overheating. Stop and let it cool before driving on.

P0606.m: The engine computer found a fault in its own processor. Stalling or limp mode can follow.
c: Poor power or ground to the module

U0140.t: Lost Communication With Body Control Module
U0140.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the body control module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the body control module

P0732.m: Second gear isn't matching the expected engine-to-wheel speed, which usually means slipping in that gear.

P0106.t: Manifold Absolute Pressure/Barometric Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
P0106.m: The MAP sensor reading doesn't fit what the engine is doing.

P0868.m: Transmission fluid pressure is too low, which can cause slipping or loss of drive.

P2119.t: Throttle Actuator Control Throttle Body Range/Performance
P2119.m: The throttle isn't reaching the position it's commanded to.

P0731.m: First gear isn't matching the expected engine-to-wheel speed, which usually means slipping in that gear.

P2101.t: Throttle Actuator A Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
P2101.m: The electronic throttle motor isn't responding correctly. The car may drop into reduced power.

U0073.t: Control Module Communication Bus A Off
U0073.m: A data network the car's computers share has gone quiet.

P06DD.t: Engine Oil Pressure Control Circuit Stuck Off
P06DD.m: Oil pressure isn't reaching what the computer asked for; the variable oil pump may be stuck in its low-pressure mode. Check the oil level and have the oil pressure tested right away.

P2122.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch D Circuit Low
P2122.m: One of the gas pedal position signals reads too low, so the car may go into reduced power.

P0440.m: The system that traps fuel vapor from the gas tank has a fault. It's an emissions problem, not usually a drivability one.

P0607.m: The engine computer isn't performing correctly.

U0402.m: Another computer in the car received data from the transmission computer that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the transmission computer

P0089.m: The fuel pressure regulator isn't holding the pressure the computer asks for. Stalling and hesitation are common.

P0500.m: The computer lost the vehicle speed signal. The speedometer, cruise control and shifting can act up.
c: ABS sensor fault on some cars

P0733.m: Third gear isn't matching the expected engine-to-wheel speed, which usually means slipping in that gear.

P2104.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Idle
P2104.m: The computer found a throttle problem and is holding the engine at idle for safety. The car may barely move.

P0746.t: Pressure Control Solenoid A Performance/Stuck Off
P0746.m: The main transmission pressure solenoid isn't controlling pressure, so shifts can slip or flare.

U0131.t: Lost Communication With Power Steering Control Module
U0131.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the power steering control module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the power steering control module

P0780.m: A shift didn't happen the way the computer expected.

P2714.t: Pressure Control Solenoid D Performance/Stuck Off
P2714.m: Transmission pressure solenoid D isn't controlling pressure, so shifts can slip or bang.

P0734.m: Fourth gear isn't matching the expected engine-to-wheel speed, which usually means slipping in that gear.

P0841.t: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Range/Performance
P0841.m: A transmission fluid pressure reading doesn't match the gear the computer expects.

P0021.t: A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Intake, Bank 2)
P0021.m: The variable valve timing for the intake camshaft on bank 2 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P0744.t: Torque Converter Clutch Solenoid Circuit Intermittent
P0744.m: The torque converter lockup control drops out now and then.

U0416.t: Invalid Data Received From Vehicle Dynamics Control Module
U0416.m: Another computer in the car received data from the stability control module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the stability control module

P0336.m: The crankshaft position signal is erratic. The engine can stumble, stall or be hard to start.

P0369.t: Camshaft Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1)
P0369.m: The second cam sensor signal on bank 1 drops out now and then.

P0446.t: Evaporative Emission System Vent Control Circuit
P0446.m: The EVAP vent valve isn't working right.

P0711.t: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0711.m: The transmission fluid temperature reading doesn't make sense.

P0496.t: Evaporative Emission System High Purge Flow
P0496.m: Too much fuel vapor is being pulled into the engine, often from a purge valve stuck open. It can cause hard starts after fueling.

P050A.t: Cold Start Idle Air Control System Performance
P050A.m: Right after a cold start, the idle speed isn't where the computer wants it.

P0507.t: Idle Air Control System RPM Higher Than Expected
P0507.m: The engine idles higher than it should.

P0121.m: The throttle position reading doesn't make sense for the conditions. Hesitation or reduced power is common.

P0191.t: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor A Range/Performance
P0191.m: The fuel pressure reading doesn't match what the computer expects. Hard starting or stalling can follow.

U0420.t: Invalid Data Received From Power Steering Control Module
U0420.m: Another computer in the car received data from the power steering control module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the power steering control module

P0024.t: B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Exhaust, Bank 2)
P0024.m: The variable valve timing for the exhaust camshaft on bank 2 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P0715.m: The transmission lost its input speed signal, so shifting can become harsh or stuck in one gear.

U0155.t: Lost Communication With Instrument Panel Cluster (IPC) Control Module
U0155.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the instrument cluster. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the instrument cluster

P17F0.m: On Nissans with a CVT, the transmission computer detected shudder (judder) while driving. Nissan service bulletins send this code to a transmission inspection, and some cars got a reprogram or a new CVT.

P2196.t: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2196.m: The upstream O2 sensor keeps reading rich.

P17F1.m: On Nissans with a CVT, the transmission computer detected judder. Nissan's repair steps for this code inspect the control valve (valve body) and the CVT's belt or chain.

P0725.m: The transmission computer lost the engine speed signal.

P2110.t: Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Limited RPM
P2110.m: The computer is limiting engine speed because of a throttle fault.

U0418.t: Invalid Data Received From Brake System Control Module
U0418.m: Another computer in the car received data from the brake system control module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the brake system control module

P1870.m: On GM automatics like the 4L60-E, the computer saw slipping when the torque converter clutch was told to lock up, most often from wear in the torque converter clutch valves.
c: Worn TCC regulator or isolator valve bore

P0102.t: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A Circuit Low
P0102.m: The air flow sensor signal is too low.

P2441.t: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
P2441.m: The valve that lets cold-start air into the bank 1 exhaust is stuck closed.
c: Water or carbon in the valve

P3497.m: The system that shuts off cylinders to save fuel has a fault on bank 2.

P3400.m: The system that shuts off cylinders to save fuel has a fault on bank 1. The engine can run rough or misfire.

P0365.m: The computer can't read the second (usually exhaust) cam sensor on bank 1.

P219B.m: One or more cylinders on bank 2 are getting a different air-fuel mix than the others. The engine may idle rough or hesitate.

U0151.t: Lost Communication With Restraints Control Module
U0151.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the airbag (restraints) control module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the airbag (restraints) control module

P0716.t: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0716.m: The transmission's input speed signal is erratic.

P0341.m: The bank 1 camshaft signal doesn't match what the computer expects.
c: Stretched timing chain or jumped belt

P0755.m: Shift solenoid B isn't working as commanded, so the transmission may skip gears, shift harshly or stay in one gear.

P0721.m: The transmission's output speed signal is erratic.

P0019.t: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 2 Sensor B)
P0019.m: The crankshaft and the bank 2 camshaft aren't lined up the way the computer expects. That usually points to timing chain or belt problems, so it's worth checking early before it gets worse.
c: Stretched timing chain or jumped belt

P0462.t: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Low
P0462.m: The fuel level sender reads too low. The gauge may show empty when it isn't, or the other way around.

P2004.t: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2004.m: The flaps inside the bank 1 intake manifold are stuck open. Power and smoothness can suffer.
c: Carbon buildup on the runner flaps

U0001.m: The main high-speed data network that the car's computers use to talk has a fault. Many warning lights can come on at once.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the network
A failing module dragging the network down

P050D.m: The engine idles rough right after a cold start.

P2096.t: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Lean (Bank 1)
P2096.m: After the catalytic converter, the exhaust reads too lean for too long.

P0013.t: B Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Exhaust, Bank 1)
P0013.m: The variable valve timing for the exhaust camshaft on bank 1 isn't where the computer asked it to be. The engine can idle rough, lose power or use more fuel. Low or dirty oil is a common trigger, because oil pressure moves the timing.
c: Low, old or wrong-grade engine oil

P200A.m: The intake runner flaps aren't moving as commanded.

P0520.t: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
P0520.m: The oil pressure sensor has an electrical fault. Check the real oil level before driving on.

P0234.m: The turbo is making more boost than it should, so the computer may cut power.

P00C6.t: Fuel Rail Pressure Too Low - Engine Cranking
P00C6.m: Fuel pressure is too low while the engine is cranking, so it may be slow or unable to start.

P0404.t: Exhaust Gas Recirculation A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0404.m: The EGR valve isn't moving the way it's commanded.

P0601.t: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
P0601.m: The engine computer found an error in its own memory.

P0796.t: Pressure Control Solenoid C Performance/Stuck Off
P0796.m: Transmission pressure solenoid C isn't controlling pressure.

P2757.t: Torque Converter Clutch Pressure Control Solenoid Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P2757.m: The torque converter clutch pressure control isn't working as commanded. Shudder is common.

P0562.m: The car's electrical voltage is too low. Lights and modules may act up, and the car may not start next time.

P0506.t: Idle Air Control System RPM Lower Than Expected
P0506.m: The engine idles lower than it should and may stall.

P2127.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E Circuit Low
P2127.m: The second gas pedal position signal reads too low.

P0777.t: Pressure Control Solenoid B Stuck On
P0777.m: Transmission pressure solenoid B is stuck on.

U0170.t: Lost Communication With Restraint System Sensor "A"
U0170.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from an airbag system sensor. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at an airbag system sensor

P0443.t: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit
P0443.m: The purge valve circuit has an electrical fault.

P0464.t: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0464.m: The fuel level signal drops out now and then.

P0326.m: The knock sensor signal is outside its expected range.

P0411.t: Secondary Air Injection System Incorrect Flow Detected
P0411.m: The secondary air system isn't moving the right amount of air.

P0123.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit High
P0123.m: The throttle position signal is too high.

P0344.t: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1)
P0344.m: The bank 1 camshaft signal drops out now and then.

P0122.t: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P0122.m: The throttle position signal is too low.

U0293.t: Lost Communication With Hybrid Powertrain Control Module
U0293.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the hybrid powertrain control module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the hybrid powertrain control module

U0404.t: Invalid Data Received From Gear Shift Control Module "A"
U0404.m: Another computer in the car received data from the gear shift module that did not make sense.
c: A fault inside the gear shift module

P2402.t: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit High
P2402.m: The EVAP leak test pump circuit reads too high.

P0088.m: Fuel pressure is higher than the computer wants.

P0352.m: The computer sees an electrical fault in ignition coil B (usually the coil for cylinder 2). That cylinder may misfire. If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plug overloading the coil

P0505.m: The idle control isn't holding the right idle speed.
c: Dirty throttle body or IAC valve

P0351.m: The computer sees an electrical fault in ignition coil A (usually the coil for cylinder 1). That cylinder may misfire. If the check engine light flashes, ease off and get it checked right away.
c: Worn spark plug overloading the coil

P0449.t: Evaporative Emission System Vent Valve/Solenoid Circuit
P0449.m: The EVAP vent valve circuit has an electrical fault.

P0418.t: Secondary Air Injection System Control A Circuit
P0418.m: The relay or circuit that runs the secondary air pump has a fault.

U0103.t: Lost Communication With Gear Shift Module
U0103.m: The other computers in the car stopped hearing from the gear shift module. Features that depend on it can stop working, and several warning lights often come on together.
c: Wiring or connector fault on the data network
Power or ground problem at the gear shift module

P228C.t: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low
P228C.m: The fuel pressure regulator can't keep pressure up. Stalling and power loss are common.
c: Failing fuel pump or high-pressure pump

P069E.t: Fuel Pump Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P069E.m: The fuel pump control module found its own fault and turned on the check engine light.

P0627.m: The fuel pump control circuit is open. The engine may not start or may stall.
c: Failed fuel pump relay or module

P0339.t: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0339.m: The crankshaft position signal drops out now and then, which can cause sudden stalling.

U0422.t: Invalid Data Received From Body Control Module
U0422.m: Another computer in the car received data from the body control module that did not make sense.

P0025.t: B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded (Exhaust, Bank 2)
